rationale: Submitted a probe for an unexpected local result: in the same-ballot tie-break scenario the owner's own recovery left its instance with no command and emitted no proposal, and the recorded leader bookkeeping showed only the self reply appended with no nacks, which the current account does not explain. The question and its provisional hypothesis are registered, and the two declared comparisons measure whether the instance keeps a command and whether delivery order changes the outcome; no interpretation is asserted yet.

investigations.question: Can a recovery of an instance by its own alive owner drop the instance's command when some replies at the same value ballot carry no command, and does the outcome depend on the delivery order of those replies?
investigations.hypothesis: The adoption loop takes any reply whose VBallot is >= the running candidate ballot, and the instance's fields are then overwritten with lb.cmds/lb.status before the sub-case dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1291-1296), so a reply at the same value ballot that carries no command can replace the command the owner itself contributed; the same message set delivered in a different order could then reach a different adopted value.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the recorded instance command length differs between the two delivery orders for the same reply set, and whether the owner's leader bookkeeping (appended count, nacks, dispatch) shows which reply the loop adopted.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0), replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3; replica 3 accepts without ever pre-accepting (its state holds no command), and the owner's AcceptReplies are left in flight. The owner, alive and still holding X, then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0); the harness delivers the Prepare replies of replicas 2, 3 and 4 in a chosen order (replica 2 carries X at value ballot 0, replicas 3 and 4 carry no command at the same ballot) and records whether the owner re-proposes a command and what its instance holds afterwards. The test runs the same message set twice with the empty reply last in one run and first in the other.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
Delivery order among the prepare replies is chosen by the harness, which is what a real network does not fix; the read order is not altered.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own handlers, fails replica 1 after its reply, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, then calls the owner's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers each collected PrepareReply to the owner, recording the owner's leader-bookkeeping state (status, appended count, nacks, prepared flag) and the instance's command length before and after the dispatch.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of an instance must not drop the instance's command when a reply without a command arrives at the same value ballot as replies that carry one, and the adopted value must not depend on the delivery order of equally admissible replies.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering replica's own adoption loop and dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 and 1291-1313): the replies are the acceptors' honest answers at their stored ballots.

comparisons.description: After the owner's recovery of its own instance, the instance still holds a command (its own X); violated when the instance is left with no command even though the owner's own reply carried it.

Control for delivery order: the same message set with the empty reply delivered first must leave the instance holding a command as well; a different outcome between the two orders shows the adopted value depends on arrival order rather than on the ballot.
